title: Vertical slice: rounds, end to end
content:
One module proving every pattern before the other eight are written. Deliberately narrow: create a round, list rounds, read one.

Exercises the whole stack — migration, Drizzle schema, domain entity with Result, repo port and D1 adapter returning domain entities, query port returning read-model DTOs, use-case, thin route with Zod, OpenAPI entry, container wiring, e2e tests through HTTP at 100%, deployed.

Done when:
- POST /api/v1/admin/rounds and GET /api/v1/admin/rounds work against real D1
- /openapi.json includes them, generated from the same Zod schemas
- Coverage is 100% with no v8 ignore hints
- All three gates green, deployed to dev
- A written note in the task comment on where the 100% gate hurt — that finding shapes the other eight modules

title: Establish schema conventions and the first migration
content:
Schema grows with the modules that need it. This task does NOT define all 22 tables — it fixes the patterns every future migration follows, and ships exactly one table to prove them.

Part 1 — conventions, written to docs/schema-conventions.md:
- Primary keys: UUIDv7 via the IdGenerator port, never database-generated
- Timestamps: created_at / updated_at on every table, UTC, storage format decided here
- Round scoping: which tables carry round_id and which do not, stated as a rule rather than case by case
- Locale-keyed JSON: the exact shape for admin-editable labels ({"en": "..."}), and the fallback rule
- Soft archival: archived_at everywhere on configuration, plus the partial-unique pattern (UNIQUE ... WHERE archived_at IS NULL)
- Foreign keys and cascade policy: what cascades, what restricts, what nulls
- Naming: snake_case, plural tables, <entity>_id foreign keys
- audit_log carries no PII — stated as a constraint future migrations are checked against
- Where schema files live: platform/d1/schema/<module>.ts, one per module, re-exported from an index
- The seam with better-auth: it owns user/session/account/verification and generates its own migrations. Document how our migrations order against its, and how startups.owner_user_id references its user id.

Part 2 — resolve the D1/SQLite unknowns, with evidence not assumption:
- Foreign key enforcement in D1 — on by default, or does it need a PRAGMA? This matters immediately for startups.owner_user_id crossing into better-auth's table.
- Partial unique indexes — does the WHERE archived_at IS NULL pattern work?
- Generated columns — supported? STORED vs VIRTUAL trade-offs for dynamic-field indexing (§13.3)
- json_extract performance without jsonb — acceptable at expected volume?

Record the answers in the conventions doc. Every one of these shapes migrations written months from now.

Part 3 — migration 0001: the startups table (§4.1), applying every convention above. Auth is the first thing built, so identity is the first schema to land. One founder owns one startup; all other startup profile data lives in field_values later.

Everything else — rounds, stages, fields, documents, applications, notifications, events, announcements, support, audit — arrives with its module. technical-design.md §4 remains the target model and the reference to design against; it is not a migration plan.

Done when: docs/schema-conventions.md exists and answers all four D1 questions with evidence, migration 0001 applies cleanly to a local D1 alongside better-auth's own tables, and the startups table demonstrates the id, timestamp, and foreign-key conventions.

title: Auth: OTP signup and password sign-in, end to end
content:
The first thing built. Applicants and staff can create an account and sign in.

Scope:
- POST request-otp — email, rate limited per address and per IP, Turnstile, never logs the code
- POST complete-signup — OTP + password, creates the account, proves the address, no separate verification step
- POST sign-in — email + password, server-side session, cookie scoped to the parent domain
- POST request-password-reset and reset — same OTP mechanism
- Session middleware resolving a request to a branded UserId
- Our startups row created and linked to better-auth's user id

Rules that apply:
- OTP delivery goes through the Notifier port, never a built-in mailer. Email now, phone later, same code path — see technical-design.md §12.1.
- better-auth is confined to modules/identity and http/middleware/auth.ts. No other module imports it (CONVE-15, codebase-structure.md §7).
- Everything downstream sees UserId, never a better-auth type.
- Tests go through HTTP at 100%, with port substitution only for delivery failure paths (CONVE-16).

Security, not optional: OTP single-use and invalidated on success, short expiry, attempt limits with lockout, constant-time comparison, rate limits on both OTP endpoints. An unrated OTP endpoint is free email for an attacker and a bill for you.

Done when: a user can sign up with an emailed OTP plus password and sign back in, staff accounts work through the same flow with roles deciding access, coverage is 100% with no v8 ignore hints, all three gates pass, deployed to dev.

title: Spike: better-auth on Workers — OTP signup and password hashing
content:
Throwaway code. Prove better-auth runs on Cloudflare Workers backed by D1 through Drizzle, for the specific flow sebp needs.

The flow: email -> OTP delivered -> user submits OTP + chosen password -> account created. Sign-in is email + password. Phone becomes a second OTP channel later.

Blocking questions:
- BCRYPT IS UNAVAILABLE IN WORKERS. What does better-auth actually use for password hashing on this runtime — WebCrypto PBKDF2, a WASM argon2/scrypt build, something else? Are the parameters adequate? If the answer is bad, the auth design changes and everything downstream waits.
- Does the OTP / email-verification plugin support "verify code AND set password in one step", or does it assume separate verify-then-register?
- Can OTP delivery be routed through our own Notifier port rather than a built-in mailer? Pingram is the transport and must stay behind the port.
- Does the Drizzle D1 adapter work, or does it assume node/postgres?
- What schema does better-auth own, and how does startups.owner_user_id reference it?
- Session validation cost per request — does it hit D1 every time, and can sessions live in KV?

Deliverable: a working throwaway Worker plus a written verdict in the task comment. If any blocking question fails, say so loudly rather than working around it quietly.

title: Spike: verify Pingram's API surface
content:
Confirm against Pingram's own documentation, not assumption.

Must answer:
- Auth model and how the key is held in Workers secrets
- OTP support for phone verification, or must we build it
- SMS coverage in applicant regions
- Delivery webhooks for bounce and failure — payload shape, signature verification
- Rate limits and pricing at expected volume

The Notifier port shape (§8.3) depends on this. No delivery webhooks means notification_deliveries status tracking cannot work.

title: Spike: TanStack Start on Workers reaching the API via Service Binding
content:
Throwaway code. The two-repo split is only cheap if Service Bindings work from TanStack Start server functions.

Must answer:
- Does TanStack Start deploy to Workers cleanly with wrangler?
- Can a server function reach a Service Binding, or only the fetch handler?
- Does SSR streaming survive the binding call?
- How is the binding typed and configured across two wrangler.toml files?

If server functions cannot reach the binding, the split costs a real network hop on every render and hosting should be reconsidered.

title: Bootstrap sebp-api repository
content:
Hono on Workers, empty but fully wired.

- pnpm, TypeScript strict, Hono, Zod, Drizzle, wrangler
- vitest with @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers, isolated storage per test
- Coverage thresholds at 100% (lines, functions, branches, statements)
- ESLint with no-restricted-imports and no-restricted-globals per codebase-structure.md §14
- dependency-cruiser config enforcing domain purity, barrel-only cross-module imports, better-auth confinement, no cycles
- Directory skeleton per §2, empty modules
- dev/staging/production environments with separate D1, R2, KV, Queue bindings

Done when: pnpm lint && pnpm depcruise && pnpm test all pass on an empty repo, and a hello-world route is deployed to dev.

title: Bootstrap sebp-web repository
content:
TanStack Start on Workers, empty but fully wired. Depends on the Service Binding spike.

- pnpm, TypeScript strict, TanStack Start, wrangler
- Playwright with Istanbul instrumentation of the built bundle and coverage merge
- Coverage threshold at 100%
- Route group skeleton: (public), (auth), (app), (admin)
- lib/api/client.ts as the only API caller; lib/api/generated/ wired to openapi-typescript
- Service Binding to sebp-api configured

Done when: a public SSR page renders meaningful HTML with JavaScript disabled, one Playwright test passes at 100%, deployed to dev.

title: Platform ports and composition root
content:
The seam every other module depends on. No business logic.

Ports in src/ports/: Clock, IdGenerator, ObjectStorage, KeyValueStore, JobQueue, Notifier — signatures per codebase-structure.md §6, all returning Result.

Adapters in src/platform/: R2ObjectStorage, KvStore, CfJobQueue, PingramNotifier, systemClock, uuidV7Generator. Drizzle client for D1.

shared/: Result type and helpers, branded id types, error unions.

container.ts constructing all of the above from Env.

Done when: dependency-cruiser passes, the container builds in a test, and each adapter has a failing-path test using port substitution.

title: CI pipeline with the three gates
content:
GitHub Actions for both repos: pnpm lint && pnpm depcruise && pnpm test, failing on coverage below 100%.

Also: migrations applied in CI, wrangler deploy to dev on merge to main, and openapi-typescript regeneration checked in sebp-web so a stale client fails the build.
